 Judgment
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that on 26.03.2023 at about 4.00 to 4.05 pm, petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-37-EH-4373 from Sampigehalli main Road, Hegade Nagar towards Sampigehalli side by observing traffic rules, at the same time the driver of car bearing Reg No.KA-02- ML-7076 came in opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Vishnu Kumar vs Harini Chandrashekar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19350540/
1 the petitioner's motor cycle dut to which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
That he was admitted to Hosmat hospital, Bengaluru and found that he sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery.
He was working as Executive Engineer and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the accident he lost the income.
He is unable to work as earlier.
He has spent Rs.15,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
The accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing reg.No.KA-02-ML-7076.
The respondent is the owner is liable to pay the compensation.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation along with interest and costs in the above case.

3. On issuance of notice to the respondent appeared through her counsel and has filed written statement contending that (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.4318/2023 petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
She denied the accident and manner of accident alleged by the petitioner.

She stated that the petitioner was a rash driver and was trying to over haul all passing by and in which he over hauled an auto and flashed toward respondent's husband who was driving the said car bearing reg No.KA-02-ML-7076.

The respondent's husband being in all control tried to avoid the mishap and turned toward left but unfortunately the petitioner being not in control of the vehicle due to over taking with high speed bagged in to the right front portion of the respondent's car due to the sudden harsh hit the respondent cars air bag opened up and the car was dragged to the right lane where it ended up crashing into electric pole.
Hence, respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
Medical treatment and expenses alleged are denied.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds she prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this court has framed the following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 26.03.2023 at bout 4 to 4.05 PM he was riding motor cycle bearing No.KA-37-EH- 4373 from Sampigehalli main road towards Sampigehalli side, by observing traffic rules at that time one car bearing No.KA-02-ML- 7076 came from opposite side driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and hit the two wheeler of the petitioner and (SCCH-12) 4 MVC.No.4318/2023 petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4. What Order or Award?
5. To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex.P.1 to P.26 documents are marked on his behalf.

Doctor by name Nagaraj.B.N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Senter,

The medical record officer by name Shanthamma.S got examined as PW.3 and through him Ex.P.29 to 35 documents are marked.
Respondent is examined as R.W.1.
Through her Ex.R.1 to R.8 documents are marked.

She did not tender herself for cross examination hence, cross of R.W.1 is taken as nil and respondent evidence is closed.
6.
Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.

7. On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3:
Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order, for the following;
 (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.4318/2023  REASONS 8.

ISSUE NO.1: To prove that petitioner sustained injuries due to RTA on 26.03.2023 at 4.00 to 04.05 pm by rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No.KA-02-ML-7076, petitioner entered into the witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
He reiterated petition averments in his chief examination.
He has produced FIR, copy of complaint, sketch, spot panchanama, IMV notice and answer to it, IMV report, wound certificate, final report and discharge summaries at Ex.P.1 to 12.

On perusal of those documents it can be seen that one Rajeshwari who is wife of the petitioner has given first information to Hennur police station stating that her husband Vishnu Kumar was riding his motor cycle on 26.03.2023 on Sampegehali Main road, towards Hegadenagar to Sampigehalli, at that time, driver of one car bearing No.KA-02-ML-7076 who was drunk and driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to her husband's motor cycle, due to which Vishnu Kumar fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

That he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital,
Bengaluru and he is undergoing treatment, therefore action may be taken against the driver of car.
9. On the basis of this first information received by Hennur police Crime No.23/2023
is registered against the driver of car No.KA-02-ML-7076 for the offence p/u/s 279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.185 of IMV Act.
The sketch produced at Ex.P.3 shows petitioner was coming in the straight direction and car came to extreme right side and hit the bike of the petitioner.
The spot (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.4318/2023 panchanama shows that the road is a two-way tar road, does not have a center median.
There is no tyre marks or broken parts of the vehicle on the spot.

Wound certificate shows that, petitioner sustained right distal femur fracture open type 3A,
right mid shaft tibia fracture closed and he was admitted with the history of RTA two Vishnu Kumar vs Harini Chandrashekar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19350540/

As per the final report driver of the Car found to be negligent and also drunk at the time of accident and charge sheet is filed against him.
Even against the car owner there is charge of having no insurance at the time of accident u/Sec.196 of IMV Act.

10. On perusal of these documents it can be seen that as per the case of petitioner, he was moving in straight direction while the car driver having drunk came in rash and negligent manner hit the petitioners bike and petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
11. On the contrary the respondent owner contended that petitioner himself was negligent and was trying to overtake the vehicles.

It is also stated that, husband of the respondent tried to take control of the vehicle but due to the act of the petitioner,
accident took place.
To prove the said fact owner appeared before the court and got examined as R.W.1.

She has produced 4 photos, CD, vehicle damage job card,
Certificate u/s 64B of Indian Evidence Act which are marked at Ex.R.1 to 8.
She has not tendered herself for cross examination.
Mere averments made in the chief examination without subjecting her to cross examination are not reliable.
During the course of arguments petitioner contended that respondent and the driver have (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.4318/2023 pleaded guilty before the court of competent jurisdiction.
The written statement averments and the documents produced by the respondent are not proved by giving complete evidence.
The respondent and the car driver have not questioned the FIR, final report or any other police documents.
The final report shows the driver was drunk at the time of driving the car therefore though respondent contended that, driver of the car tried to control the vehicle could not be believable.
As such, in the opinion of this court on the basis of oral and documentary evidence, petitioner has proved the driver of Car bearing No.KA-02-ML-7076 was negligent in driving the car.
Accordingly I answer this issue in the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age, petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P13 which shows that he was born in year of 1991.
Accident took place on 26.03.2023.
Respondent disputed the age of the petitioner but no satisfactory evidence is placed to prove his age.
He was aged 32 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 32 years at the time of accident.
13. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was an Executive Engineer and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
To prove his earnings petitioner has not produced any document.
Hence, notional income has to be considered Rs.16,000/- per month and same is considered as his monthly income.
14. In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name Nagaraj.B.N, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.4318/2023 Senter, Bangalore is examined as P.W.2.

sentences.text:
In his chief examination he stated that petitioner has sustained left proximal tibia fracture, right femur,
Vishnu Kumar vs Harini Chandrashekar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19350540/
4 supracondylar fracture, right tibia shaft fracture type III A right patella undisplaced fracture.
Surgery was conducted in the form of ORIF with LCP and right tibial nailing on 27.03.2023 and other injuries were treated conservatively.
P.W.2 has assessed physical disability of 58% of right lower limb and 37% of whole body.
15. In the cross examination it is suggested that, at the time of discharge, petitioner was healthy.
P.W.2 admitted the same.
As per the evidence of doctor petitioner has whole body disability of 19%.
Doctor can assess only physical disability and not the functional disability.

Considering the occupation of the petitioner as Executive Engineer, no document being produced to show his occupation, no document available that he has left the job or he was demoted due to injuries sustained by him, in the opinion of this court there is no functional disability which affects the income of the petitioner.
Accordingly functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is held as NIL and Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the car bearing No.KA-02-ML-7076.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence, he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondent.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
 (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.4318/2023 (i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.17.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.5,12,582/- as per Ex.P.17 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by prescriptions of the doctor.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.5,12,582/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted in Hosmat hospital from 26.03.2023 and discharge on 01.04.2023 and has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.11.
Further he was again admitted on 09.03.2024 and discharged on 11.03.2024 and has produced discharge summary at Ex.P12.
He was in hospital for almost 10 days.
Accident took place in the year 2023.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 10 days = Rs. 5,000/-is awarded.
(iii) Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 10 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2023, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 10 days =Rs.5,000/-is awarded.

5 (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.4318/2023 (iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.16,000/-.
He suffered 4 injuries which are grievous in nature.
He was inpatient for 10 days and he was advised to take rest.
Minimum 4 months is required to recover from such grievous injury.

Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 4 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000/-x 4= Rs.
64,000/-
He is entitled to Rs.64,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner took treatment at Hosmat hospital.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Hence, conveyance charges of Rs.5,000/- is awarded.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2, there is no functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner.
Accordingly no compensation is awarded under this head.

(vii) For Future medical expenses: P.W.2 doctor who has assessed the disability of the petitioner has stated that petitioner needs to removal the implants which may require Rs.1,20,000/- but no estimation is produced.
In view of necessity of removal of implants for well being of the petitioner in the opinion of this court amount of Rs.40,000/- shall be awarded for future medical treatment.
Accordingly, Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
(SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.4318/2023 (viii) For Pain and sufferings
: The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
The records show that he underwent operation.
He was in hospital for 10 days and he underwent surgery therefore, he sustained pain and sufferings.
For pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of treated doctor,
petitioner complained about difficulty in waling on slope, climbing stairs, standing on affected legs,
squatting, sitting cross legs, difficulty in kneeling and take turns also, he cannot walk fast and run.
He suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and come in the way of normal enjoyment of life.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.60,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:
As per the evidence of assessed doctor, petitioner complained about pain and restriction in movement but there is no specific evidence regarding future prospects loss of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.7,41,582/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
17. ISSUE NO.4:-
In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hand of Respondent.

Since there was no insurance policy as on the date of accident, respondent is personally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.7,41,582/- with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment excluding future medical expenses.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following :
 (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.No.4318/2023  ORDER  The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,41,582/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.7,01,582 /- from the date of petition till the date of payment.

(Future medical Vishnu Kumar vs Harini Chandrashekar on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19350540/
7 expenses of Rs.40,000/- will not carry interest).
The respondent is liable to pay compensation to petitioner and she is hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.
The petitioner is entitled to have release of entire amount without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled to compensation from the hand of Respondent.

Since there was no insurance policy as on the date of accident, respondent is personally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner to the tune of Rs.7,41,582/- with interest @ of 6% from the date of petition till the date of payment excluding future medical expenses.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following :
 (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.No.4318/2023  ORDER  The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,41,582/- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.7,01,582 /- from the date of petition till the date of payment.
The respondent is liable to pay compensation to petitioner and she is hereby directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within 2 months from the date of this order.
The petitioner is entitled to have release of entire amount without making F.D.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
